title: The real TMC test, all 30 questions
subtitle: The computer-based test as it was actually set: same 30 questions, same order, same five styles, one mark each.
note: Reconstructed from the captured test and its verified answer key. The questions, their styles, their order and their answers are exactly as recorded; some scenario wording is paraphrased where the capture was partial. It predates Lecture Five, so nothing here covers Module 5.

questions.prompt: Q1. A student has a bold ambition but no way of proving progress toward it. Applying the OKR framework, what should he do?

options.text: Replace the ambition with something smaller and safer
List every activity he intends to perform this quarter
Separate the ambitious qualitative vision from measurable Key Results, then tie those Key Results to specific outcomes rather than activities
Set a single annual deadline and review it at the end of the year

questions.explanation: An Objective is qualitative and ambitious; Key Results are measurable outcomes. Activities describe what you do, Key Results describe what changes.

questions.prompt: Q2. Which statements match the lecture on reputation and mentorship? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Reputation is built in ordinary moments through reliability and integrity
Do not wait to be assigned a mentor; pursue one and show you are already in motion
Reputation is made mainly in dramatic, high-visibility moments
A mentor should be approached only after you have achieved something significant

questions.explanation: Reputations are built in the ordinary moments, and you pursue a mentor by demonstrating you are already in motion.

questions.prompt: Q3. Match each behaviour to the branding concept it demonstrates.

pairs.left: Saying no to opportunities outside your domain
Building genuine relationships rather than collecting contacts
Delivering excellence and integrity when nobody is watching
Choosing one go-to area within your field

questions.explanation: Focus, cultivation, deposits, niche. The two decoys are real concepts from Slides 8 and 14.

questions.prompt: Q4. Which statements about the SWITCH protocol and fear are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: SWITCH works mainly through the placebo effect of expecting improvement
Fear is best managed by accepting it and waiting for it to pass
SWITCH builds new neural structures through deliberate practice, not motivational self-talk
Fear neurologically suppresses the prefrontal cortex, so creative capacity itself is diminished

questions.explanation: New neural structures, and genuine suppression of the prefrontal cortex. Both a and b are the passive readings the lecture rejects.

questions.prompt: Q5. The 12-Week Year raises follow-through compared with annual planning because short, repeated cycles keep urgency psychologically active.
questions.explanation: With twelve months the brain behaves as though there is always more time. Twelve-week cycles keep urgency alive.

questions.prompt: Q6. Match each description to the OKR component it defines.

pairs.left: Effort that cannot be measured as an outcome
Stable across cycles and motivates over the long term
Measurable outcomes that prove the objective was reached
A bold qualitative statement answering "Where am I going?"

questions.explanation: Activity, Vision, Key Results, Objective. The activity row is the distinction the exam tests most.

questions.prompt: Q7. A student keeps failing to do his weekly planning. Implementation Intentions help because {{1}} A correctly written example is {{2}} The cue matters because {{3}} And the research shows {{4}}

accept: they use a specific formula to pre-decide behaviour so the future self does not negotiate
choices: they use a specific formula to pre-decide behaviour so the future self does not negotiate
they increase motivation by making the goal more exciting
they remove the need for any planning at all

accept: "When I sit down at my desk on Monday at 6 PM, I will complete my weekly planning worksheet"
choices: "When I sit down at my desk on Monday at 6 PM, I will complete my weekly planning worksheet"
"When I feel ready, I will complete my weekly planning worksheet"
"I will try to do my weekly planning every Monday"

accept: it must be concrete: a time, a place or a completed action, never vague or emotional
choices: it must be concrete: a time, a place or a completed action, never vague or emotional
it must be emotionally meaningful so that it motivates action
it should change weekly to prevent boredom

accept: people who specified exactly when and where followed through 71% of the time against 32% with intention only
choices: people who specified exactly when and where followed through 71% of the time against 32% with intention only
people who wrote goals down achieved them 95% of the time
people who shared goals with a partner were 76% more likely to achieve them

questions.explanation: Pre-decision, a concrete cue, and 71% against 32%. The final decoys are the 95% and 76% figures from other slides.

questions.prompt: Q8. A student wants to prepare mentally for a high-stakes presentation. Which actions match the lecture? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Wait until the fear subsides naturally before rehearsing
Deliberately practise visualisation to prime the brain for the result
Use the SWITCH protocol to externalise doubts and replace them with rehearsed positive self-talk
Accept that presentation anxiety is fixed and work around it

questions.explanation: Visualisation primes the brain; SWITCH externalises and replaces. Options a and d are the passive stance the lecture rejects.

questions.prompt: Q9. A newly hired department head is designing systems for her team. She knows they need {{1}} She implements this by {{2}} She also ensures they have {{3}} She further addresses {{4}}

accept: a clear vision with precision: specific targets to run toward, not vague directions
choices: a clear vision with precision: specific targets to run toward, not vague directions
a motivational culture that keeps morale high
more staff, since capacity is the real constraint

accept: establishing written quarterly goals where each person knows exactly what they are after
choices: establishing written quarterly goals where each person knows exactly what they are after
holding daily meetings to discuss progress informally
asking each person to set whatever goal they prefer

accept: the right tools and knowledge, which is Kit 4, for their domain-specific work
choices: the right tools and knowledge, which is Kit 4, for their domain-specific work
a larger budget before any work begins
external consultants to design the process

accept: Kit 5, timing for when execution will be most effective, and Kit 6, persistent tillage for sustainable results
choices: Kit 5, timing for when execution will be most effective, and Kit 6, persistent tillage for sustainable results
Kit 1, task, and Kit 2, training, which are the only kits that matter to a manager
Kit 7, tarrying, alone, since waiting is the whole discipline

questions.explanation: This question links four Kits at once: Target, Tools, Timing and Tillage.

questions.prompt: Q10. Match each description to the concept it names.

pairs.left: Fear suppresses the prefrontal cortex
The subconscious accepts what is repeatedly impressed upon it
Fear is a cognitive stance to be replaced, not managed
A state enabling exploration, incompatible with fear

questions.explanation: Four concepts from Stages I and S of the W.I.S.E. Model.

questions.prompt: Q11. An entrepreneur considers launching without proper preparation. The lecture's teaching suggests {{1}} Its practical advice is {{2}} The Spanner metaphor {{3}} and the King metaphor {{4}}

accept: this is like going to war without arms: you will expend effort but achieve nothing
choices: this is like going to war without arms: you will expend effort but achieve nothing
speed matters more than preparation in a competitive market
preparation is useful but optional if the idea is strong

accept: acquire the tools, meaning knowledge, mentors, resources and proven frameworks, no matter the cost
choices: acquire the tools, meaning knowledge, mentors, resources and proven frameworks, no matter the cost
borrow whatever tools are cheapest and upgrade later
begin first and acquire tools as problems arise

accept: illustrates that trying a task without the right tool causes wasted effort
choices: illustrates that trying a task without the right tool causes wasted effort
shows that persistence eventually loosens any bolt
proves that strength matters more than equipment

accept: teaches that a wise leader consults and prepares before committing to battle
choices: teaches that a wise leader consults and prepares before committing to battle
teaches that a king must never retreat once committed
shows that authority removes the need for counsel

questions.explanation: War without arms, acquire at any cost, the Spanner on wasted effort, the King on consulting first (Luke 14:31).

questions.prompt: Q12. Match each description to the element of the system it names.

pairs.left: Persistent, humble cultivation, letting results grow over time
The clear, specific target you are running toward
Seasons change and readiness must align with action timing
Acquiring the specific tools, knowledge and resources for your domain

questions.explanation: Tillage, Target, Timing, Tools.

questions.prompt: Q13. A manager does not believe her team is capable, and her plans keep failing. In W.I.S.E. terms, what must change first?

options.text: Her Spirit, the belief system, must be realigned through deliberate rewiring so that faith in her team's capability can emerge before execution
Her Execution, since better tools would solve the problem regardless of belief
Her Wisdom, since she simply needs more information about her team
Nothing internal; she should replace the team

questions.explanation: Peale fuels the engine. A mind rebuilt but filled with doubt will not generate the energy execution demands.

questions.prompt: Q14. "When I feel stressed, I will take a break to reset" is a properly formed Implementation Intention.
questions.explanation: "When I feel stressed" is an emotional and vague cue. A proper cue is a time, a place or a completed action.

questions.prompt: Q15. Kit 5 in the systems framework addresses {{1}} The lecture teaches that {{2}} Jesus' own practice models this: {{3}} The principle is {{4}}

accept: Timing: understanding the seasons and readiness for when execution will be most effective
choices: Timing: understanding the seasons and readiness for when execution will be most effective
Tillage: the quality of labour you put into the work
Tarrying: the discipline of waiting after the work is done

accept: to every thing there is a season, and right timing is a major asset
choices: to every thing there is a season, and right timing is a major asset
timing is outside your control and therefore not worth studying
the earliest mover always holds the advantage

accept: he said "Mine hour is not yet come" at Cana, and with Lazarus he waited two days so the outcome would be resurrection, not healing
choices: he said "Mine hour is not yet come" at Cana, and with Lazarus he waited two days so the outcome would be resurrection, not healing
he acted immediately in every recorded case to model urgency
he delegated the timing of his works to his disciples

accept: until the time is ripe, do not step out, because right timing is a major asset
choices: until the time is ripe, do not step out, because right timing is a major asset
step out early and correct course as you go
wait indefinitely until every risk has been removed

questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 3:1, John 2:4 at Cana, and the two-day wait for Lazarus that produced resurrection rather than healing.

questions.prompt: Q16. An ambitious student has a compelling vision and a strong work ethic but keeps shifting priorities to whatever is trending. His mentor says, "You're fighting the air instead of running at the tape." What is this pointing to?

options.text: He is not reading enough industry publications
His work ethic is insufficient compared with more successful peers
He lacks the networking connections to succeed
The absence of a clear, written goal targeting a specific outcome, so his actions lack aim and dissipate effort

questions.explanation: Without a target you copy what is popular and end up disjointed.

questions.prompt: Q17. Adaeze sets an OKR to become a credible emerging voice in digital media. Her Key Results include {{1}} At quarter end her scores were {{2}} Her overall score was {{3}} and the value of scoring is that {{4}}

accept: publishing 12 posts with a minimum of 200 views each, and securing 2 active industry mentors
choices: publishing 12 posts with a minimum of 200 views each, and securing 2 active industry mentors
attending networking events regularly and reading industry blogs
building her confidence and improving her writing style

accept: posts 0.75, having published 9 of 12, and mentors 0.5, having found 1 of 2
choices: posts 0.75, having published 9 of 12, and mentors 0.5, having found 1 of 2
posts 0.9, having published 11 of 12, and mentors 1.0, having found 2 of 2
posts 0.5, having published 6 of 12, and mentors 0.75, having found 1 of 2

accept: 0.76, rated Strong, reflecting weighted performance across all Key Results
choices: 0.76, rated Strong, reflecting weighted performance across all Key Results
0.75, rated Adequate, taken from her weakest Key Result
1.0, rated Excellent, since the objective was broadly achieved

accept: it replaces vague guilt with a structured conversation about what changes next quarter
choices: it replaces vague guilt with a structured conversation about what changes next quarter
it determines whether the objective should be abandoned
it ranks her against her classmates

questions.explanation: 12 posts at 200 views, 2 mentors, scores 0.75 and 0.5, overall 0.76 Strong.

questions.prompt: Q18. Why does the 12-Week Year outperform annual planning?

options.text: Twelve-week goals are inherently easier than annual ones
It removes the need for weekly review
Short, repeated timelines keep urgency psychologically active, while annual timelines allow procrastination because the brain perceives an abundance of time
It replaces goals with habits, which require no planning

questions.explanation: Urgency is low in January, relevance fades in June, panic arrives in October.

questions.prompt: Q19. "Hold daily check-ins" and "run weekly workshops" are well-formed Key Results.
questions.explanation: They are activities. They describe what you do rather than what changes as evidence of progress.

questions.prompt: Q20. A final-year student is deciding whether to specialise. The lecture teaches that {{1}} The answer to that question {{2}} And the critical question to settle before graduation is {{3}}

accept: choosing a niche is a launch pad, not a limitation, which lets you build depth and become sought after
choices: choosing a niche is a launch pad, not a limitation, which lets you build depth and become sought after
choosing a niche narrows your options and should be delayed as long as possible
specialisation matters only in technical fields

accept: determines your positioning strategy, your visibility, and whether you are remembered for something specific
choices: determines your positioning strategy, your visibility, and whether you are remembered for something specific
determines only which modules you should take next semester
has little effect once you have a good degree classification

accept: "What is the one area within my field where I want to be the go-to person?"
choices: "What is the one area within my field where I want to be the go-to person?"
"Which employer in my field pays the most?"
"How many fields can I credibly claim competence in?"

questions.explanation: Launch pad not limitation; positioning, visibility and recall; and the one go-to area.

questions.prompt: Q21. An entrepreneur has studied his field, invested in tools and prepared extensively, yet has not launched because he waits for "the perfect time". The lecture answers with a direct principle: {{1}} It further warns that {{2}} A football match {{3}} and the lecture {{4}}

accept: without a clear goal or target you have nothing to aim at; you fight the air instead of running at the tape
choices: without a clear goal or target you have nothing to aim at; you fight the air instead of running at the tape
without perfect conditions you should indeed wait, since timing is everything
without a mentor no launch can succeed

accept: when you lack a written goal you unconsciously copy what is popular or what others do
choices: when you lack a written goal you unconsciously copy what is popular or what others do
when you lack a written goal you simply work more slowly
when you lack a written goal you become more adaptable

accept: without goalposts never ends, just as success without clear targets is impossible to achieve
choices: without goalposts never ends, just as success without clear targets is impossible to achieve
without spectators has no meaning, just as success needs an audience
without a referee becomes unfair, just as success needs oversight

accept: emphasises running with the tape as your target, with precision and clarity
choices: emphasises running with the tape as your target, with precision and clarity
emphasises waiting until every uncertainty is resolved
emphasises copying whichever approach is currently succeeding

questions.explanation: Fighting the air, copying what is popular, no goalpost no game, running with the tape.

questions.prompt: Q22. Which actions match the lecture's advice on building a professional presence? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Collect as many contacts as possible so that your network is large
Cultivate relationships with people doing work that matters
Spread across several domains so you are never boxed in
Select one domain and build depth in it

questions.explanation: Options a and c are the two traps: collecting contacts, and the generalist spreading thin.

questions.prompt: Q23. Match each contribution to the source it comes from.

pairs.left: A unified framework of wisdom, instruction, spirit and execution
Belief and experience are causally linked; fear and faith cannot coexist
A 21-day rewiring protocol
Fear suppresses the prefrontal cortex

questions.explanation: The model, Peale, SWITCH, Leaf. The decoys are the two Execution authors.

questions.prompt: Q24. Because a niche limits the opportunities available to you, the lecture advises against specialising too early.
questions.explanation: A niche is a launch pad, not a limitation. Specialising is encouraged.

questions.prompt: Q25. A professional does excellent, reliable work but is known only to the few colleagues she works with directly. In Brand Bank terms, what is her problem?

options.text: Her deposits are too small to matter
She is making withdrawals without realising it
She has confused packaging with substance
Her deposits are strong but invisible: her reputation reaches only those she works with, not the broader market that could refer her

questions.explanation: The greatest threat to your brand is not failure, it is invisibility.

questions.prompt: Q26. Reviewing Adaeze's quarter, the scoring shows {{1}} This matters because {{2}} The end-of-quarter figure {{3}} and overall the system {{4}}

accept: some Key Results scored 0.75, being 9 of 12 posts, and others scored 1.0, such as the internship, creating a nuanced overall score of 0.76
choices: some Key Results scored 0.75, being 9 of 12 posts, and others scored 1.0, such as the internship, creating a nuanced overall score of 0.76
every Key Result scored the same, giving a flat result
only the lowest Key Result was counted, giving 0.5

accept: it allows a structured conversation about what changes next quarter rather than vague guilt or shame
choices: it allows a structured conversation about what changes next quarter rather than vague guilt or shame
it identifies who on the team should be replaced
it proves whether the objective was worth setting

accept: of 0.76, rated Strong, reflected weighted performance and substantial progress even where full achievement was not reached
choices: of 0.76, rated Strong, reflected weighted performance and substantial progress even where full achievement was not reached
of 0.76 was a failure, since anything under 1.0 means the objective was missed
of 0.76 was an average of the highest two Key Results

accept: replaces vague guilt with structured conversation and enables continuous improvement
choices: replaces vague guilt with structured conversation and enables continuous improvement
rewards only those who achieve every Key Result in full
discourages ambitious objectives because they score lower

questions.explanation: 0.75 and 1.0 producing 0.76 Strong, and scoring as a structured conversation rather than guilt.

questions.prompt: Q27. On the necessity of a personal target, the lecture teaches that {{1}} It illustrates the danger: {{2}} It insists that {{3}} and it advises {{4}}

accept: without a goal you cannot score one, just as a football match without goalposts never ends
choices: without a goal you cannot score one, just as a football match without goalposts never ends
without a goal you will still succeed if you work hard enough
without a goal you remain flexible, which is an advantage

accept: one person starts a crusade, another opens a shop, a third returns to school, and without a personal target you follow all of them and become disjointed
choices: one person starts a crusade, another opens a shop, a third returns to school, and without a personal target you follow all of them and become disjointed
people with targets often choose the wrong ones and waste years
following others is efficient because it reduces risk

accept: always asking "What am I actually after?" is essential for coherent direction
choices: always asking "What am I actually after?" is essential for coherent direction
asking what others are doing is the fastest way to decide
direction matters less than effort in the long run

accept: running with the tape as your target, with precision
choices: running with the tape as your target, with precision
beating the air until an opportunity presents itself
waiting for a clearer season before choosing a target

questions.explanation: No goalpost no game, the disjointed follower, what am I actually after, and running with the tape.

questions.prompt: Q28. Which activities are effective deposits in the Brand Bank Account? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Posting frequently on social media about your ambitions
Attending every event in your industry
Delivering committed work on time with excellence on every project, not just the visible ones
Maintaining integrity when unwatched and treating "unimportant" people with respect

questions.explanation: Deposits are excellence, integrity, fulfilled promises and showing up consistently. Volume of posting and attendance are neither.

questions.prompt: Q29. Walking through the SWITCH protocol in order: {{1}} {{2}} {{3}} and the whole protocol {{4}}

accept: after Gathering awareness and Focused Reflection on the root cause, they Write the thought to externalise it
choices: after Gathering awareness and Focused Reflection on the root cause, they Write the thought to externalise it
after Writing the thought they Gather awareness of where it came from
after Celebrating progress they Gather the next toxic thought

accept: next they Revisit the pattern to see connections and understand context, then engage in Active Reach to choose and rehearse the replacement thought
choices: next they Revisit the pattern to see connections and understand context, then engage in Active Reach to choose and rehearse the replacement thought
next they Reach out to a friend for support, then Revisit the thought a week later
next they Rest from the thought entirely and allow time to pass

accept: finally they Celebrate their growth and reinforce the new pathway through acknowledgment
choices: finally they Celebrate their growth and reinforce the new pathway through acknowledgment
finally they record the outcome and repeat the cycle immediately
finally they discard the journal so the thought is not revisited

accept: is designed to build new neural structures through deliberate practice and repetition over 21 days
choices: is designed to build new neural structures through deliberate practice and repetition over 21 days
is designed to distract the mind until the thought fades on its own
works by suppressing the toxic thought whenever it appears

questions.explanation: Gather, Focused Reflection, Write, Revisit, Active Reach, Celebrate, over 21 days, building new neural structures.

questions.prompt: Q30. Repeating daily affirmations is sufficient on its own to achieve what the SWITCH protocol achieves.
questions.explanation: SWITCH is a full six-step rewiring protocol, not motivational self-talk.
